Stated Claim / Post Context:
Victory for Serbian democracy, breakthrough PTSD treatment, nurses win paid parental leave in Pittsburgh

In today's edition: the populist right-wing leader of Serbia has been ousted after 12 years of power in a democratic election, a newly FDA-cleared treatment for PTSD sees a 68% rate of remission, and Pittsburgh nurses have secured the USA's first countywide 12-week paid parental leave policy.

Actual Article Body:
Squirrel News Team | Posted on October 26, 2026 |

Photo: Stefan Kostić/Unsplash (CC0)

In today’s edition: the populist right-wing leader of Serbia has been ousted after 12 years of power in a democratic election, a newly FDA-cleared treatment for PTSD sees a 68% rate of remission, and Pittsburgh nurses have secured the USA’s first countywide 12-week paid parental leave policy.

The long-serving populist right-wing leader of Serbia, Aleksandar Vučić, has conceded defeat, ushering in a seismic political shift after a historic election that saw ​the increasingly authoritarian leader pitted against a student-led movement that had spent two years protesting against his government.

Source: The Guardian

The win comes as Brazil remains a crucial bulwark against the global rise of the far right. As far-right parties and leaders have gained ground across Latin America and Europe, Brazil has defied the trend. Lula has also been continuously decreasing deforestation levels in the Brazilian Amazon, and has pledged to end the practice by 2030.

Source: The Conversation

A newly FDA-cleared treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder combines personalised brain mapping with magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity. In a clinical trial, the approach reduced symptoms by 52%, with 68% of participants seeing remission.

Source: Science Daily

The vaccine, intismeran, is custom-made to target genetic mutations unique to an individual’s melanoma. It is the first individualised cancer vaccine to show positive results in a phase III clinical trial. The trial found that at two years post treatment, the combination of intismeran and pembrolizumab reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% compared with treatment with pembrolizumab alone.

Source: The Guardian

After seeing parents forced back to work while their newborns remained in intensive care, nurses in Pittsburgh launched a campaign for change. Their efforts helped secure the USA’s first countywide policy guaranteeing 12 weeks of paid parental leave.

Source: 19th News

New York City is expanding its free childcare programme for 2-year-olds, adding an extra 10,000 seats for fall 2027. The expansion will bring the 2-K programme to more neighbourhoods, including every community in the Bronx and Staten Island, giving more families access to early childhood education.

Source: ABC7NY

Australia’s New South Wales state government has approved a conservation park along the Mid North Coast. The new park will merge existing national parks, state forests and other public land, placing areas previously used for logging under conservation protection.

Source: ABC

In an unexpected discovery, scientists found that bleached coral can recover when placed in contact with a healthy genetic clone. The damaged coral regained its health so completely that it became virtually indistinguishable from its healthy counterpart. The findings could offer new insights into coral recovery and help inform efforts to protect vulnerable reef ecosystems.

Source: CBC

Designed to reduce outdoor water use, the Florida-Friendly Landscaping Incentive Program helps eligible residents convert irrigated turfgrass into water-efficient landscapes. Participants can replace up to 500 square feet of grass with drought-resistant plants, including native species that thrive in dry conditions, conserve water, and provide habitat for local wildlife.

Source: 93.3 FLZ

Once a year, Corvo, the smallest and most northerly island of Portugal’s Azores archipelago, goes dark. Since 2019, the island’s 450 or so inhabitants have chosen to switch off the lights every autumn for five nights to tackle the disastrous effects of artificial light on Cory’s shearwaters, a seabird endemic to the Atlantic Ocean.

Source: The Guardian
